mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level above 1900 thousand units consistently precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong residential construction signals robust consumer spending and economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1900 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate borrowing and equity valuation compression.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of housing starts above 1900 thousand units and CPI inflation below 200 index produces positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days, as low inflation supports consumer spending growth without triggering aggressive monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 1900 and CPIAUCSL < 200.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 typically delivers negative 20-day returns due to reduced consumer confidence and corporate profit expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production level above 105 index (2017=100) signals robust manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as supply chain strength supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 105.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI inflation exceeds 200, the S&P 500 typically experiences negative 60-day returns due to the expectation of central bank rate hikes and reduced real equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 200.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 200) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 delivers negative 20-day returns as monetary tightening suppresses risk appetite and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 200.

mechanism_narrative: A labor force employment level above 130,000 thousand persons consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, reflecting strong economic conditions and consumer spending power.
